content:
A resort, hotel or homestay near Pune (in Lonavala, Khandala, Mahabaleshwar, Panchgani, Mulshi, Kamshet or Tamhini) gets more direct bookings by doing four things in order: making its own website a better place to book than an online travel agency (OTA) listing, with live availability, clear prices and a booking engine that works on a phone; getting that rate into Google through Hotel Center and free booking links so it appears beside OTA prices in search; keeping its Google Business Profile, photos and reviews strong; and only then spending on ads, mainly to bring back people who already looked. As a digital marketing agency in Pune, we see properties try to buy direct bookings with Instagram ads while their own site has no booking engine and a rate higher than the OTA's. The ads cannot fix that.

This guide is for owners and managers of independent resorts, boutique hotels, villas and homestays within a weekend drive of Pune and Mumbai. It covers why direct bookings matter, how to make the website and booking engine competitive, how Google's hotel search and free booking links work, what to do on the Business Profile, how to use Meta and Google ads sensibly, and how to measure whether any of it worked.

## Why direct bookings matter, and why OTAs still have a place

OTAs bring guests you would never reach on your own, especially first-time visitors and travellers from other cities. They also take a commission on every booking (the percentage depends on your contract and the programmes you join; check yours), own the guest's contact details, and set the terms on cancellations and promotions.

A direct booking:

- costs you less per booking, even after ad spend, when the campaign is set up well;
- gives you the guest's contact details and consent to stay in touch, so a repeat stay costs nothing to win;
- lets you offer packages (meals, activities, early check-in) the way you want.

The realistic goal for most independent properties is not to leave OTAs. It is to move repeat guests, weekend regulars and people who already found you on Google to direct booking, while OTAs keep bringing new guests.

## Step 1: Make your website the best place to book

### A booking engine, not an enquiry form

If your website's "Book now" opens a form or a WhatsApp chat, many guests will check availability on an OTA instead, because the OTA answers instantly. A booking engine shows live availability and price for the selected dates, takes the booking, and sends a confirmation. Most booking engines connect to a channel manager, which keeps inventory in sync across your website and every OTA, so you do not double-book the last room on a long weekend.

What to look for in a booking engine:

- **Works well on a phone.** Most leisure bookings start on mobile; test the full flow on an inexpensive Android phone over mobile data.
- **Shows the full price before the last step,** including taxes and any mandatory charges. Surprises at the end lose bookings and erode trust.
- **Room and package display** with photos, occupancy, bed type, meal plan and cancellation terms for each rate.
- **Channel manager connection** to the OTAs you use.
- **Google connectivity:** check whether the engine or its channel manager is an integrated Google connectivity partner, which matters for free booking links (Step 2).
- **Tracking:** the engine should let you measure completed bookings in Google Analytics 4 and pass conversions to ad platforms. Many engines run on their own domain, which breaks tracking unless set up properly (cross-domain measurement in GA4).

### Rate parity and what you can offer directly

OTA contracts often include rate parity clauses, and the rules differ by contract. Read yours. Within whatever your contract allows, common ways to make direct booking better without undercutting the public rate are:

- included breakfast or a meal;
- flexible cancellation;
- early check-in or late check-out when available;
- a welcome activity or a discount on spa or activities;
- member or returning-guest rates for people who sign in or book again.

Show these benefits beside the booking widget: "Book direct: breakfast included, free cancellation up to 72 hours".

### Pages that sell a stay

- **Rooms and villas:** one page per room type with honest photos, size, view, bed configuration, occupancy and amenities.
- **Packages:** weekend getaway, monsoon, family, corporate offsite, wedding and events, with what is included.
- **Location and directions:** drive time from Pune and Mumbai, route, road conditions in monsoon, parking, nearest station. This page often ranks for searches like "[place] resort how to reach".
- **Things to do nearby,** written by someone who has done them: treks, forts, lakes, viewpoints, with distances and seasons.
- **Policies:** check-in and check-out times, ID requirements, pets, children, cancellations, quiet hours, outside food and alcohol rules.
- **Photo and video gallery,** compressed and fast; a [virtual tour](/services/virtual-tours) helps guests understand villa layouts and event spaces.

Write each page for the guest, not for keywords. A page titled "Monsoon getaway at our Mulshi resort: rooms, rates and what to expect in July" that answers real questions (do the roads flood? is the pool open? are there power cuts?) will do more than "Best resort near Pune".

## Step 2: Get your price into Google with Hotel Center and free booking links

When someone searches for your property by name, or looks at hotels in an area on Google Search or Maps, Google shows a booking module with prices from different sites. Your own website can appear in that list as "Official site" through **free booking links**, which Google says it shows without any fee from the hotel.

How it works in practice:

- Google needs a feed of your rates and availability. For most independent properties, that comes from a **connectivity partner**: a booking engine, channel manager or property management system integrated with Google.
- Through the partner you get a **Hotel Center** account linked to your property's Business Profile, where you can see reporting on free booking link clicks and bookings.
- If your current booking engine is not a connectivity partner, Google maintains a partner list; it may be worth switching engines for this alone.

Why it matters: guests comparing your listing on Google see the official site price beside the OTA prices. If your direct rate is the same and comes with breakfast, a good share of them will click your site. If your official site is not listed at all, every one of those clicks goes to an OTA.

Google also runs paid Hotel Ads through Google Ads. Most small properties should get free booking links working and measured before considering paid hotel campaigns.

## Step 3: Make the Google Business Profile do its job

For hotels, the Business Profile is often the first thing a traveller sees. It shows photos, reviews, amenities, location, and the booking module. Work through:

- **Correct category** (Resort hotel, Hotel, Guest house, Homestay or similar, whichever genuinely fits) and accurate address and pin.
- **Amenities and attributes,** kept accurate: pool, Wi-Fi, parking, pet-friendly, restaurant, air conditioning.
- **Photos** that show what guests will actually find: rooms, bathrooms, views, the pool, the food, the approach road. Update seasonally; monsoon greenery sells well, but winter guests should see the property as it looks in winter.
- **Reviews:** ask every guest at check-out, without offering incentives, and reply to every review, including the critical ones. Google's policies forbid incentivised and selectively solicited reviews.
- **Questions and messages:** answer quickly, or turn them off if no one can monitor them.

Our guide to [optimising your Google Business Profile](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-google-business-profile-optimisation-categories-services-photos-2026/) covers categories, services and photos in detail.

## Step 4: Use ads to bring back people who already looked

Only once the website books well and Google shows your official rate does paid advertising make sense. For an independent property, budgets are usually small, so spend where intent is high.

### Brand search on Google

People search for your property by name and click OTA ads that appear above your listing. A small Google Ads campaign on your own brand name, sending people to your website with your direct-booking benefits in the ad text, often has the best return of any ad you can run. Keep it tightly limited to your brand terms. Our [Google Ads service](/services/google-ads) can set this up with proper booking conversion tracking.

### Remarketing

Many people visit a resort's website, check dates and leave to talk to family. Remarketing ads on Meta and Google bring them back with the dates they looked at, a seasonal offer, or the direct-booking benefits. Build audiences from website visitors and booking-engine abandoners, with consent handled correctly; our guide to [building remarketing audiences on Google and Meta](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-remarketing-audiences-consent-2026/) explains how.

### Meta for awareness and packages

Instagram and Facebook work well for showing the property: reels of the view, the pool, the food, a monsoon morning. Use them to build an audience around specific packages (monsoon weekends, New Year, corporate offsites) and target people in Pune and Mumbai who are likely to drive. Point ads to the package page with the booking widget, not to the home page. Many properties also run Click-to-WhatsApp ads for groups, events and weddings, where guests want to talk before booking; see our guide to [Click-to-WhatsApp ads and lead tracking](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-click-to-whatsapp-ads-lead-tracking-2026/).

### Timing for Pune-area properties

Demand around Pune follows clear patterns: monsoon weekends from June to September, Diwali and Christmas to New Year, long weekends, and school holidays. Plan campaigns three to six weeks before each peak, when people are planning, not the week of the weekend when inventory is already full. Midweek stays and corporate offsites are where ads can fill rooms that would otherwise stay empty.

## Step 5: Keep guests coming back

Direct bookings get cheaper with every repeat guest. With consent:

- collect email and WhatsApp opt-in at booking;
- send a thank-you after the stay with a link to leave a review;
- send a short message before the next season the guest is likely to return (a monsoon guest is probably a monsoon guest again);
- offer a returning-guest rate on your website.

A simple guest database, ideally in a [hotel CRM](/services/hotel-crm) connected to the booking engine, lets you see who stayed, when and how often, and avoid sending the same offer to everyone. Keep the messaging rare and relevant.

## Measuring what works

Without measurement, a property cannot tell whether the agency's "great engagement" turned into bookings. Track:

- **Direct bookings and revenue per month,** from the booking engine.
- **Share of bookings by channel:** direct, each OTA, walk-in and phone.
- **Free booking link clicks and bookings,** from Hotel Center.
- **Ad spend per direct booking,** by campaign.
- **Commission saved** compared with the same bookings on an OTA, which is the real return.
- **Repeat guest share.**

A monthly one-page report with these numbers tells you more than any number of reach and impression figures.

## A worked illustration

Consider a hypothetical eight-room resort in the Mulshi area that gets most of its bookings through two OTAs, with a website that only has an enquiry form. A sensible plan:

1. **Month 1:** choose a booking engine with a channel manager and Google connectivity; rebuild room, package and location pages; add direct-booking benefits.
2. **Month 2:** activate free booking links; tidy the Business Profile; start a review-request routine at check-out; set up GA4 cross-domain tracking and booking conversions.
3. **Month 3:** start a brand search campaign and website remarketing; prepare monsoon package content and Meta ads for the season.
4. **Every month after:** report direct share, cost per direct booking and commission saved.

We cannot promise a specific direct-booking share; it depends on location, reviews, pricing and the competition. What the plan does is remove the reasons a guest who already wants your property would book it through someone else.

## What it typically costs

Indicative ranges, not a quotation:

- **Booking engine and channel manager:** usually a monthly subscription, sometimes with a per-booking fee; pricing varies widely by vendor and property size.
- **Website rebuild or upgrade** for a small property with booking engine integration, room and package pages and tracking: roughly ₹60,000 to ₹2,00,000.
- **Ongoing digital marketing management** (Business Profile, brand search, remarketing, Meta content and reporting): roughly ₹20,000 to ₹60,000 a month, plus ad spend, depending on scope.
- **Photography and video:** priced separately; good visuals often move results more than any ad setting.

## Frequently asked questions

### How can a small resort get more direct bookings instead of OTA bookings?

Add a mobile-friendly booking engine with live availability to your website, offer direct-booking benefits such as breakfast or flexible cancellation within your OTA contract, get listed on Google's free booking links so your official price appears in search, keep the Google Business Profile and reviews strong, and use brand search and remarketing ads to bring back people who already looked.

### What are Google free booking links for hotels?

They are unpaid listings in Google's hotel booking module that show a property's official site, or other booking sites, with prices beside paid hotel ads. Google says it charges no fee for them. A property usually joins through a connectivity partner, such as its booking engine or channel manager, which sends rates to Google, and sees results in Hotel Center.

### Do I need a booking engine if I already take bookings on WhatsApp?

For most leisure properties, yes. Many guests want to see availability and the full price instantly; if they have to wait for a reply, they often book through an OTA. WhatsApp remains useful for groups, events and questions, alongside the booking engine.

### Should a resort run Google Ads on its own brand name?

Often yes, when OTAs bid on your property name and appear above your listing. A small, tightly limited brand campaign that sends people to your website with direct-booking benefits can recover bookings that would otherwise pay commission. Measure it against booking-engine conversions.

### When should resorts near Pune start advertising for the monsoon season?

Plan campaigns three to six weeks before demand peaks, so for monsoon weekends from June to September, start preparing content and ads in May. The same applies to Diwali, Christmas and New Year and long weekends.
